display.en: Have you ever wondered where rain comes from? The water you drink today might once have been part of a cloud, an ocean or even a dinosaur's puddle. Water moves around our planet in a big loop called the water cycle.

display.en: Part 1: Evaporation.

spoken.en: Part one: Evaporation.

display.en: The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers. When water gets warm, tiny bits of it rise into the air as an invisible gas called water vapor. This is called evaporation.

spoken.en: The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers. When water gets warm, tiny bits of it rise into the air as an invisible gas called water vapor. This is called evaporation.

display.en: Plants help too. They let out water from their leaves, a little like sweating.

spoken.en: Plants help too. They let out water from their leaves, a little like sweating.

display.en: Key takeaway: The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers.

headline.en: The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers.

display.en: Part 2: Condensation.

spoken.en: Part two: Condensation.

display.en: High in the sky, the air is cold. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Millions of these drops crowd together and make a cloud.

spoken.en: High in the sky, the air is cold. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Millions of these drops crowd together and make a cloud.

display.en: You can see condensation at home. When you pour a cold drink, little drops appear on the outside of the glass.

spoken.en: You can see condensation at home. When you pour a cold drink, little drops appear on the outside of the glass.

display.en: Key takeaway: You can see condensation at home.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: You can see condensation at home.

headline.en: You can see condensation at home.

display.en: Part 3: Precipitation.

spoken.en: Part three: Precipitation.

display.en: When the drops in a cloud get too big and heavy, they fall to the ground. We call this precipitation. It can be rain, snow, sleet or hail.

spoken.en: When the drops in a cloud get too big and heavy, they fall to the ground. We call this precipitation. It can be rain, snow, sleet or hail.

display.en: Key takeaway: We call this precipitation.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: We call this precipitation.

display.en: Part 4: Collection.

spoken.en: Part four: Collection.

display.en: The water that falls collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and even under the ground. Then the sun warms it up again, and the whole cycle starts over.

spoken.en: The water that falls collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and even under the ground. Then the sun warms it up again, and the whole cycle starts over.

display.en: Key takeaway: The water that falls collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and even under the ground.

display.en: The water cycle never stops. Every raindrop, snowflake and puddle is part of the same amazing journey.
